deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the draft of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847). It was published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke (1876, ed. Weber/Dedekind). In that essay a 'derivative' (Ableitung) of arbitrary order ∂_x^ν z is defined through a generalized Taylor expansion.

Series (1) is the ordinary Taylor series: z(x+h) = Σ_{n≥0} (d^n z/dx^n) h^n / n!.

Series (2) is the general ansatz: z(x+h) = Σ_ν K_ν ∂_x^ν z · h^ν. Here ν runs over an arithmetic progression with step 1 (ν = p+n, n∈Z), unbounded in both directions. K_ν is a coefficient function still to be chosen.

The page has no computations. It is a programmatic paragraph.

(a) It closes the preceding remark (the 'Protestation') against the blanket condemnation of divergent series. That remark arose from formula (3) on p.12: x^μ/Π(μ) = Σ_{α∈p+Z} b^{μ−α}/Π(μ−α) · (x−b)^α/Π(α). For a negative integer μ the left side vanishes, so one gets nontrivial (divergent) series of this form that represent 0.

(b) It states the requirement that ordinary differentiation be a special case of the Ableitung. This holds as soon as K_ν = 1/(1·2···ν) for nonnegative integers ν (K_0 = 1 is tacitly included) and K_ν = 0 for negative integers ν. Then, for integer ν, series (2) collapses to the Taylor series (1).

(c) It observes two kinds of freedom.
- Infinitely many functions K_ν satisfy this interpolation condition. My note: the eventual choice is K_ν = 1/Π(ν) = 1/Γ(ν+1), which automatically vanishes at negative integers.
- One may not assume that an expansion of a given function in given powers of h is unique. The coefficient system is not determined by the value, precisely because of the zero-representing series noted in (a). So infinitely many coefficient systems must be admitted.

The next page uses this freedom to impose further laws. Comparing d/dh and d/dx of the series gives K_{ν+1}(ν+1) ∂^{ν+1}z = K_ν d(∂^ν z)/dx.
errors: 'ganzen positiven Werthe' should strictly read 'nonnegative': K_0 = 1 is needed for the n=0 Taylor term. This is a harmless imprecision.

The claim that coefficient systems are non-unique rests on formal manipulation of divergent bilateral series. Example: for μ a negative integer, formula (3) becomes a bilateral geometric-type series that diverges for every x and equals 0 only formally, by summing each half via analytic continuation. This is heuristic, not rigorous, though it is consistent with Riemann's stated stance on divergent series.

results.what: Requirement that the generalized expansion z(x+h)=Σ K_ν ∂^ν z h^ν reduce to Taylor's series: K_n = 1/n! for n≥0 and K_n = 0 for n<0, leading to the choice K_ν = 1/Γ(ν+1)
results.modern_name: Generalized Taylor series for fractional derivatives (Riemann–Liouville calculus; cf. later Hardy/Osler generalized Taylor series)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1847 (publ. 1876); Liouville 1832 for the fractional calculus generally

results.what: Non-uniqueness of expansions in non-integer power progressions; series of this form summing (formally) to zero; defense of divergent series
results.modern_name: Non-uniqueness of bilateral fractional power series / complementary function in Riemann's fractional calculus
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Versuch..., 1847/1876); the complementary-function issue was discussed later by Cayley (1880)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of the draft of Riemann's 1847 essay on generalized differentiation, which was published in his Gesammelte Werke. The content (the conditions on K_ν and the non-uniqueness remark) is already known as his. It is purely programmatic text with no new computation.

checkable.asserts: K_ν = 1/Γ(ν+1) equals 1/ν! at nonnegative integers (all entries 0).
1/Γ(ν+1) vanishes at negative integers ν = -n-1 (equivalently 1/Γ(s)=0 at s=0,-1,-2,...), as required for series (2) to reduce to (1).
Reflection identity used to show the μ=-1 case of formula (3) gives terms -(sin(πα)/π) b^(-1-α)(x-b)^α (result 0).
The two halves of the bilateral series Σ_{n∈Z}(-r)^n, each summed by analytic continuation, cancel to 0. This is the formal zero-series behind the non-uniqueness claim (result 0).

transcription_corrections: Line 'für alle ganzen negativen[?] Werthe': the image shows 'negativen' written with a deletion/overwrite mark at its start, but the intended reading 'negativen' is correct.
'nur eine Entwicklung' and 'nur ein System': the words 'eine'/'ein' are underlined in the manuscript (emphasis), with 'eine' apparently overwritten/struck and rewritten.
The page number at top right is '13'; '8' in the right margin is the folio/archival number.
